title: VesselReady: domestic commercial vessels (AMSA) and Queensland recreational boats
notes: First sourced rules for VesselReady. Built from AMSA, Federal Register of Legislation (Marine Order 504, as made), Queensland Government and Maritime Safety Queensland pages read on 2026-10-09. Every reference is UNVERIFIED and carries a summary, not the source's wording: staff must capture each source, replace the extract with the exact text and verify it. The National Law, Exemption 02 and Exemption 03 schedules and Marine Orders 503 and 505 are not encoded.

documents.title: Is it a domestic commercial vessel?
You have a domestic commercial vessel—what you need to do to operate it
Obtain and display a unique vessel identifier
Marine Order 504 (Certificates of operation – national law) 2024 (F2024L01458), as made
Step 2: Check eligibility for a simplified SMS

references.section: 2. What do you use your vessel for?
references.extracted_text: [Summary, not the source's wording] A vessel used for a commercial, governmental or research activity within Australia's exclusive economic zone is a domestic commercial vessel, even if it is also used recreationally. A vessel used only for recreation is not, and is regulated by the state or territory. Foreign, defence and regulated Australian vessels, and some vessels of community groups, schools and sports bodies, are excluded.
references.interpretation: Business use of a vessel inside the EEZ generally makes it a domestic commercial vessel under the Marine Safety (Domestic Commercial Vessel) National Law. Captured on 2026-10-09 from a reading of the published page; the exact wording was not copied. Replace this with the source's own text, capture a snapshot and verify before relying on it.

references.section: 1. Your vessel; 2. Your vessel operations; 3. Your crew
references.extracted_text: [Summary, not the source's wording] Unless an exemption applies, a domestic commercial vessel needs a displayed unique vessel identifier, a certificate of survey, a certificate of operation and a safety management system, and its crew need certificates of competency. A safety management system is needed even when the vessel is exempt from a certificate of operation.
references.interpretation: Lists the core obligations for operating a domestic commercial vessel. Captured on 2026-10-09 from a reading of the published page; the exact wording was not copied. Replace this with the source's own text, capture a snapshot and verify before relying on it.

references.section: How to display your unique vessel identifier
references.extracted_text: [Summary, not the source's wording] AMSA issues a unique vessel identifier automatically with a first application for a certificate of survey, a non-survey approval or a specific exemption, or a notice of intention to build; otherwise there is a standalone application. It must be displayed within 21 days of issue (before launch for a vessel being built), above the waterline on both sides, readable from 30 metres.
references.interpretation: Every domestic commercial vessel needs a UVI, with limited exceptions (tenders, vessels on the Shipping Register, some small vessels that need one but need not display it). Captured on 2026-10-09 from a reading of the published page; the exact wording was not copied. Replace this with the source's own text, capture a snapshot and verify before relying on it.

references.section: Do I need a certificate of survey?
references.extracted_text: [Summary, not the source's wording] Every domestic commercial vessel needs a certificate of survey unless it is exempt under Exemption 02 or Exemption 40. A new vessel applies with Form 521; AMSA lists the surveys required (usually plan approval, construction and commissioning surveys) done by an accredited marine surveyor, or a recognised organisation for most vessels of 35 metres or more. A certificate is normally valid for five years.
references.interpretation: The default is that a certificate of survey is required; exemptions are the exception. Captured on 2026-10-09 from a reading of the published page; the exact wording was not copied. Replace this with the source's own text, capture a snapshot and verify before relying on it.

references.extracted_text: [Summary, not the source's wording] Without applying: human-powered vessels (including canoes and kayaks with an electric motor of 24 V or 3.5 kW or less), sailing vessels under 7.5 m with no engine or one of 3.5 kW or less, and personal watercraft under 4 m. With AMSA approval (Form 579): Class 2, 3 and 4 vessels under 12 m operating only in smooth or partially smooth (D or E) waters, Class 2 carrying no more than 4 day passengers; not for dangerous goods, primary towage, inboard engines using fuel with a flashpoint below 60 °C, or overnight hire and drive. Being exempt from survey does not remove the UVI, certificate of operation or SMS obligations.
references.interpretation: Read with Exemption 02 (current compilation in force from 1 January 2026), whose Schedule 1 was not read for this summary. Captured on 2026-10-09 from a reading of the published page; the exact wording was not copied. Replace this with the source's own text, capture a snapshot and verify before relying on it.

references.extracted_text: [Summary, not the source's wording] A certificate of operation is needed before operating a domestic commercial vessel unless an exemption applies (Exemption 03 and others). New applications, variations and added vessels use Form 504; renewals use Form 553. A certificate does not transfer to a new owner.
references.interpretation: The default is that a certificate of operation is required. Captured on 2026-10-09 from a reading of the published page; the exact wording was not copied. Replace this with the source's own text, capture a snapshot and verify before relying on it.

references.extracted_text: [Summary, not the source's wording] From 1 July 2025 no certificate of operation is needed for: tenders, sailing vessels under 7.5 m, human-powered vessels, dragon boats, Class 2 or 3 personal watercraft, some bait-gathering and training vessels under 7.5 m, and any Class 2 or 3 vessel under 7.5 m operating only in smooth or partially smooth (D or E) waters and carrying no passengers. Class 1 vessels are never eligible. A safety management system is still required.
references.interpretation: Further conditions are in Schedule 1 of the exemption, which was not read for this summary. Captured on 2026-10-09 from a reading of the published page; the exact wording was not copied. Replace this with the source's own text, capture a snapshot and verify before relying on it.

references.extracted_text: [Summary, not the source's wording] An application for a certificate of operation includes a written statement that each vessel has a safety management system complying with the order. Schedule 1 sets what the SMS covers: vessel and contact details, risk assessment, owner's and master's statements, a designated person, crewing, induction and drills, first aid and radio, operating procedures and a drug and alcohol policy, emergency preparedness, incident follow-up, maintenance, logbooks and records, and review. Schedule 2 adds requirements for Class 4 hire and drive.

references.extracted_text: [Summary, not the source's wording] All domestic commercial vessels must have a safety management system documenting how the general safety duties are met, based on a risk assessment developed with the owner, operator, master and crew. New requirements apply from 1 June 2025.
references.interpretation: An SMS is required for every domestic commercial vessel, including those exempt from a certificate of operation. Captured on 2026-10-09 from a reading of the published page; the exact wording was not copied. Replace this with the source's own text, capture a snapshot and verify before relying on it.

references.extracted_text: [Summary, not the source's wording] A simplified SMS may be used for Class 2 vessels under 7.5 m carrying 0 to 4 day passengers and Class 3 and 4 vessels under 7.5 m, unless the vessel carries dangerous goods, has lifting gear or deck loads that could affect stability, has an inboard engine using fuel with a flashpoint below 60 °C, has berthed accommodation, is set up for towage, or AMSA has found it unsuitable. rule_sets.title: Australia: domestic commercial vessels
rule_sets.description: The UVI, certificate of survey, certificate of operation, safety management system and master's certificate a vessel used for business needs, and the main exemptions, from AMSA's guidance and Marine Order 504.
limitations: Built from AMSA guidance pages and the as-made text of Marine Order 504 (2024), not from the National Law or the exemption instruments' schedules.
Doesn't check every condition of Exemptions 02 and 03 (for example dangerous goods, towage, lifting gear, tenders, heritage, training and emergency service vessels) or Exemption 40.
Doesn't decide the vessel's survey frequency category, crewing numbers or which certificate of competency each crew member needs.
Smooth and partially smooth water boundaries are set by each state; we rely on your answer.
Vessels operating beyond the exclusive economic zone are regulated Australian vessels under the Navigation Act 2012 and are not covered.
Not legal advice. Confirm with AMSA, an accredited marine surveyor or a marine safety professional before you rely on it.

rules.title: Domestic commercial vessel
rules.notes: Effective from the date the source was read (2026-10-09), not the date the law began: capped at likely until the reference is verified.

outcomes.title: Your vessel is likely a domestic commercial vessel
outcomes.detail: Using a vessel for business inside Australia's exclusive economic zone generally makes it a domestic commercial vessel under the National Law, which AMSA administers. That brings the certificates below, unless an exemption applies.

rules.title: Unique vessel identifier
rules.notes: Effective from the date the source was read (2026-10-09), not the date the law began: capped at likely until the reference is verified.

outcomes.title: Get a unique vessel identifier (UVI)
outcomes.detail: Domestic commercial vessels need a UVI, displayed within 21 days of issue. AMSA issues one automatically with your first certificate of survey or non-survey application; otherwise apply for one on its own.

approval.pathway: Issued with your first survey application, or apply separately

outcomes.title: Keep your UVI displayed
outcomes.detail: Your vessel already has a UVI. Keep it displayed on both sides above the waterline, readable from 30 metres, and tell AMSA within 14 days if you sell the vessel.

outcomes.title: You will probably need a UVI
outcomes.detail: Domestic commercial vessels need a unique vessel identifier. Tell us whether the vessel has one.

rules.title: Certificate of survey
rules.notes: Effective from the date the source was read (2026-10-09), not the date the law began: capped at likely until the reference is verified.

outcomes.title: You need a certificate of survey
outcomes.detail: From your answers the vessel doesn't fit AMSA's non-survey categories (for example it is 12 metres or longer, goes beyond sheltered waters, carries more than 4 passengers, is hired overnight or has a petrol inboard), so it needs a certificate of survey before it operates.

approval.pathway: Apply with Form 521; an accredited marine surveyor does the surveys

evidence.title: Plans and stability information your surveyor asks for
Commissioning survey report from an accredited marine surveyor

outcomes.title: A certificate of survey may not be needed
outcomes.detail: From your answers the vessel may fit one of AMSA's non-survey categories under Exemption 02. Some apply automatically (small sailing and human-powered vessels, personal watercraft under 4 metres); others need AMSA's approval first. Check the conditions before relying on this.

outcomes.title: A certificate of survey may be needed
outcomes.detail: Most domestic commercial vessels need a certificate of survey. Answer the questions about length, operating area, passengers and engines so we can check the exemptions.

rules.title: Non-survey vessel approval
rules.notes: Effective from the date the source was read (2026-10-09), not the date the law began: capped at likely until the reference is verified.

outcomes.title: Apply for non-survey approval instead of a certificate of survey
outcomes.detail: Class 2, 3 and 4 vessels under 12 metres that stay in smooth or partially smooth waters, carry no more than 4 passengers and meet the other conditions can operate without a certificate of survey once AMSA approves them under Exemption 02.

payload.task: Apply to AMSA for non-survey approval (Form 579)

rules.title: Certificate of operation
rules.notes: Effective from the date the source was read (2026-10-09), not the date the law began: capped at likely until the reference is verified.

outcomes.title: You need a certificate of operation
outcomes.detail: From your answers the vessel isn't in one of the Exemption 03 groups (for example it carries passengers, is hired out, is 7.5 metres or longer or goes beyond sheltered waters), so it needs a certificate of operation from AMSA before it operates.

evidence.title: Statement that the vessel has a safety management system that meets Marine Order 504

outcomes.title: A certificate of operation may not be needed
outcomes.detail: From your answers the vessel may be in one of the Exemption 03 groups (for example a small sailing or human-powered vessel, or a Class 2 or 3 vessel under 7.5 metres in sheltered waters carrying no passengers). You still need a safety management system. Check the exemption's conditions before relying on this.

outcomes.title: A certificate of operation may be needed
outcomes.detail: Most domestic commercial vessels need a certificate of operation. Answer the questions about length, operating area, passengers and activities so we can check the exemption.

rules.title: Safety management system
rules.notes: Effective from the date the source was read (2026-10-09), not the date the law began: capped at likely until the reference is verified.

outcomes.title: You need a safety management system
outcomes.detail: Every domestic commercial vessel needs a safety management system (SMS) that meets Marine Order 504, even if it is exempt from a certificate of operation. You write it yourself, with your master and crew; AMSA can ask to see it at any time. Use the SMS builder on this project.

approval.pathway: Write it with the SMS builder and keep it current

rules.title: Simplified safety management system
rules.notes: Effective from the date the source was read (2026-10-09), not the date the law began: capped at likely until the reference is verified.

outcomes.title: You may be able to use AMSA's simplified SMS
outcomes.detail: Vessels under 7.5 metres (Class 2 with no more than 4 day passengers, Class 3 and Class 4) may use a simplified SMS with fewer parts, unless they carry dangerous goods, have lifting gear or berthed accommodation, are set up for towing or AMSA has found them unsuitable. AMSA's pages differ on whether day passengers are allowed, so check with AMSA.

rules.title: Certificate of competency for the master
rules.notes: Effective from the date the source was read (2026-10-09), not the date the law began: capped at likely until the reference is verified.

outcomes.title: The master needs a certificate of competency
outcomes.detail: Whoever is in command needs a near coastal certificate of competency. For inshore work on a vessel under 12 metres (inboard engines under 500 kW) that can be Coxswain Grade 1 near coastal; going further out or bigger engines needs a higher certificate.

approval.pathway: Training, sea service and an AMSA practical assessment

outcomes.title: The master needs a certificate of competency
outcomes.detail: Whoever is in command needs a near coastal certificate of competency. For a vessel of 12 metres or more but under 24 metres that is at least Master less than 24 metres near coastal; larger vessels need higher certificates.

approval.pathway: Training, sea service and an AMSA practical assessment

outcomes.title: The master needs a certificate of competency
outcomes.detail: Whoever is in command of a domestic commercial vessel needs a near coastal certificate of competency; which one depends on the vessel's length, engines and where it goes.

rule_sets.title: Queensland: boat registration and licences
rule_sets.description: Recreational boat registration and marine licences in Queensland, and where commercial vessels fit, from Queensland Government and Maritime Safety Queensland pages.
limitations: Built from Queensland Government web pages, not from the Transport Operations (Marine Safety) Act or regulation.
Doesn't cover tenders, hire boats' licence arrangements, school and community vessels (Queensland regulated ships), or boats from other states visiting Queensland.
Not legal advice. Check with Maritime Safety Queensland before you rely on it.
